title: Client-led bimodal resume and chunk reconciliation for lossy mobile networks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce tail failures and user-visible truncation for streaming SSE responses on unstable mobile networks by implementing a client-first resume protocol plus chunk reconciliation that preserves function-call atomicity and structured JSONL outputs.
background: Mobile clients experience intermittent connectivity and NAT churn that lead to partial event delivery or duplicate fragments. Current server-side resume tokens assume symmetric connectivity and cause either data loss or duplication which breaks function-call atomicity and downstream structured parsers. Multiple previous tickets addressed server resume and fragmentation, but we need a lightweight client-forward approach that works across hosted and private deployments and is compatible with legacy clients.
proposal_summary: Introduce a client-led 'bimodal resume' mode negotiated at stream start. The server will emit stable chunk envelopes; the client keeps a short 'session shadow' (recent chunk metadata) and on reconnect can ask for either a delta reflow (missing chunk list) or a replay window. Reconciliation uses idempotent chunk IDs and optional compact bloom-summaries to limit server work. Ensure function-call messages remain atomic by treating 'funccall' chunks as single reconciliation units and never slicing into internal call payloads. Add SDK support for JavaScript and Python to perform incremental stitch-and-verify with optional checksum acceptance and fallbacks to full replay.
technical_spec: Chunk envelope: newline-delimited JSONL inside SSE data frames. Envelope fields: seq:number, chunk_id:hex(16), is_final:boolean, funccall_boundary:boolean, schema_version:1, resume_hint:opaque string. At stream open client and server negotiate mode via header X-Redwood-Stream-Mode: bimodal | server-resume | legacy. Client retains last N=64 envelopes (shadow) and computes a 256-bit rolling digest and a compact bloom summary for chunk_ids. On reconnect client sends POST /v1/streams/{session}/resume {"mode":"client-delta","last_seq":1234,"bloom":<base64>,"digest":<hex>} as application/json. Server responds with one of: 1) delta list of missing chunk envelopes (preferred) 2) replay window from seq X to now 3) full-session replay. Server must guarantee that any funccall_boundary:true chunk is delivered atomically; if a funccall spans multiple internal tokens, server marks the first chunk in boundary and last chunk with is_final=true and marks intermediate chunks with funccall_boundary:false but linked to the same chunk_id. Checksum verification: each chunk carries sha256 of payload; client verifies on stitch. If verification fails, SDK will request replay window that covers the failed chunk's seq-1..seq+K where K=3 by default.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (JS + Python) implement shadow buffer + reconnect POST and automatic reconciliation
Server supports X-Redwood-Stream-Mode negotiation and returns delta/replay choices
Function-call atomicity preserved: no partial funccall emitted to structured-output parser after reconnection
End-to-end integration tests with simulated 20% packet loss and random disconnects show <0.1% truncated outputs across 10k runs
Performance: server CPU overhead for delta computation < 3% p95 on a 4 vCPU test harness compared to baseline replay-only path
Telemetry: new metrics emitted (resume_mode, delta_hits, delta_cost_ns, verify_failures) and dashboards created
test_plan: Unit tests for chunk envelope encoding/decoding and sha256 verification
Integration test: JS SDK + server in-cluster with tc/netem to inject delays and drops
Load test: 10k concurrent short streams (avg 3s) with 5% reconnects, measure CPU and tail latency
Fuzz test: mutate chunk payloads to trigger verify failure and confirm fallback to replay window
Backward compatibility test: legacy client without X-Redwood-Stream-Mode must continue to work with server-resume fallback
rollout_plan: Feature guarded behind runtime flag 'client_bimodal_resume' and console toggle per-customer. Stage 1: internal dogfood (redwood-internal) with SDK opt-in. Stage 2: gradual rollout to 10% hosted traffic; monitor verify_failures and delta_hits. Stage 3: enable by default for regions with >30% mobile traffic. For Dedicated/Private customers provide explicit opt-in and documentation for KMS/HSM policies on resume_hint handling.
implementation_notes: Server: add lightweight in-memory chunk index with LRU and computation of bloom per session; persist resume_hint for audit logs
SDK: shadow buffer size configurable; default 64 envelopes and default K=3 retry window
Compatibility: if server cannot compute delta within 50ms, fallback to replay window to bound client latency
Security: resume_hint is opaque but must be logged with redaction; do not place PII in resume_hint
Telemetry: emit resume_mode negotiation events and histograms for delta size and compute latency
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete — prototype POST resume handshake and shadow buffer in JS SDK. Verified end-to-end with a local express server. — Marco
2026-03-04: Design review with PM and SDK leads. Agreed on envelope schema and negotiation header. Noted that bloom size and false-positive rate must be tuned for mobile scenarios. — Aisha
2026-03-06: Server prototype added delta path that returns up to 512 missing chunk envelopes. Observed 2.8% CPU overhead on small harness; will optimize indexing. — Marco

2026-03-09: Wrote integration test harness for randomized disconnects. Found an edge-case where intermediate chunks within a funccall were being re-applied resulting in duplicate function invocation; fixed by treating chunk_id as unit for funccall reconciliation. — Marco
2026-03-10: Ready to open PR for server delta path and JS SDK handshake. Python SDK patch in review. Planning internal dogfood next week. — Aisha
